title: Bengal CM, Jantar Mantar protest: SIT reveals arrested JeM operative's target list
content: An alleged Jaish-e-Mohammed operative was arrested by West Bengal STF. Hamim Mondal planned to target Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and disrupt a Delhi protest. He intended to disguise himself in a police uniform for sabotage activities. Mondal was in contact with Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted messaging applications. The investigation is ongoing to uncover the full extent of the terror network.

title: Rs 32 crore, boardroom feud, contract killers: How chairman plotted MD’s murder
content: A financial dispute over thirty-two crore rupees allegedly led to a murder conspiracy.  GSM Foils chairman Sagar Bhanusali is accused of hiring contract killers to eliminate his partner.  He allegedly failed to repay the large sum owed after selling his company stake.  Financial losses in stock markets reportedly pushed the chairman into debt.  Police arrested seven individuals, including the alleged shooter, in connection with the plot.

title: Samudra Manthan explained: How India’s offshore oil push can be a game-changer
content: The Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme aims to unlock India’s offshore oil and gas potential. This will be done through large-scale seismic surveys, deepwater exploration, scientific drilling.

title: Antilia bomb scare case: Court frames anti-terror charges against Sachin Waze, 9 others
content: A special court has framed charges against ten accused in the Antilia bomb scare case.  Dismissed police officers Sachin Waze and Sunil Mane face terror and murder charges.  The court observed that a case was made out by the prosecution for framing charges.  The accused pleaded not guilty to the charges brought against them.  The trial will now commence over five years after the initial incident.

title: Nuclear plants, Gaza craters: Google pulls AI tool from Google Earth in 24 hours
content: Google has removed its new AI image generation feature from Google Earth. This action followed immediate concerns raised by researchers about disinformation risks. Experts warned the tool could easily create convincing fake satellite imagery for public deception. Google stated they are implementing stronger safeguards while pausing the feature. The company noted generated images were watermarked as AI-created.

title: Ram Temple skit row: Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav booked for 'insulting Sanatan Dharma'

The opposition leaders staged a symbolic protest over alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement. This protest occurred after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced regarding temple donations. Legal action has been sought against the opposition leaders involved in the demonstration.

title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate Burmese pythons
content: Florida is employing AI-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons. These solar-powered decoys mimic prey using heat and scent to lure snakes. When a python is detected, officials are alerted to remove the invasive species. This technology complements the annual Python Challenge, which has removed thousands of snakes. These efforts aim to control the python population impacting native wildlife.

title: 'A lot of negative thoughts': Jaismine reveals how she went from hospital bed to CWG gold
content: Jaismine Lamboria won the Commonwealth Games 57kg gold medal after a significant illness. She battled a high fever and concussion during the Asian Championships earlier. This victory marked a remarkable comeback after months of uncertainty and pain. Her coaches supported her through the difficult recovery period. The gold medal fulfilled her aim of improving on her previous performance.

title: Michigan woman sues Toll Brothers over land access and wastewater plan
content: A woman from Michigan has initiated legal action against Toll Brothers concerning their wastewater management and access rights. Her property, undeveloped, is situated between two upcoming luxury housing estates. The lawsuit alleges that the developers have disregarded her property rights and neglected environmental regulations. She aims to reinstate her access easement and challenge the site plan approvals.

title: 13-year-old turns peanut shells into pesticide remover, eyes $25K prize
content: Thirteen-year-old Minnesota student Arika Kundu has designed a method that uses discarded peanut shells to help remove pesticide residues from fresh fruits and vegetables. Her project, called LIGNEX, has made her one of 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. She will now compete for the $25,000 grand prize with guidance from a 3M scientist.

title: Canada’s new Study Permit rules: An officer shall not issue visa unless these conditions are met
content: Canada has updated study permit rules, increasing financial scrutiny for applicants. Immigration officers will now examine both the amount and source of applicant funds. This change broadens the assessment beyond previous high-risk environment considerations. Applicants may need to provide additional financial and employment documents for verification. The minimum financial requirement for study permits remains unchanged by these updates.

Addressing these areas preserves functionality and market competitiveness effectively.

title: 'Sharmistha went to jail, Ruchika got away with apology': How law decides who's guilty
content: Two women faced legal action for online posts, raising questions about free speech. Sharmistha Panoli was jailed for remarks, while Ruchika Singh faces a zero FIR for alleged abuse. Harsh political remarks are not automatically criminal unless they meet specific legal elements. The article highlights the ongoing challenge of defining punishable speech in India.

title: Rahane: The silent guardian of Indian cricket whose numbers undersold his legacy

His average of 38.46 falls short of the elite, yet the numbers hide a batter who thrived overseas, delivered in crises and played defining roles in historic victories. title: India's comprehensive air defence shield designed to kill everything from drones to satellites

The nation is enhancing its capabilities with indigenous systems like Project Kusha and Akash missiles. These advancements aim to counter a wide spectrum of aerial threats effectively. India's layered defence architecture will redefine its airspace security strategy.

title: Centre's RERA extension amid Middle East conflict: What it means for homebuyers

This victory marked India's first boxing gold medal of the day.

title: More non-smokers, youth detected with lung cancer
content: Lung cancer is increasingly affecting non-smokers and young people in India. Environmental pollution and occupational exposures are significant contributing factors to this trend. Indoor air pollution also plays a role, particularly for women spending more time at home. Genetic mutations are identified as another cause, possibly triggered by lifestyle factors. Early symptoms are often overlooked, leading to delayed diagnosis and advanced disease stages.
